title: Tesla Model Y Teardown: Who Makes the Battery, FSD Chip and Tires
content:
We took the Tesla Model Y apart, part by part, and matched each part to the listed company that makes that type of component. Battery cells: LG Energy Solution, CATL, and Panasonic. FSD computer chip: Samsung Electronics. Tires: Hankook Tire. One caveat up front: Tesla has publicly disclosed its three battery suppliers, but we did not verify the chip and tire suppliers with Tesla directly — this is a map of who makes the parts, not a confirmed supplier list for every component.

Read this before the table: the three battery cell suppliers above are confirmed because Tesla itself has publicly named them. The FSD chip and tire makers are companies whose Korean business filings state they make this type of part — we found no Tesla-specific confirmation naming Samsung or Hankook for the Model Y specifically, which is why we write "makes this part," not "confirmed Tesla supplier."

1. Battery cells — three different suppliers, three different chemistries

The Model Y uses three separate battery suppliers depending on trim and production batch, all disclosed by Tesla itself.

  • LG Energy Solution supplies a 2170-format cylindrical cell (21mm diameter, 70mm height) using NCM (nickel-cobalt-manganese) chemistry, fitted to Long Range and Performance all-wheel-drive trims.
  • CATL, based in China, supplies a prismatic LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cell. LFP skips cobalt entirely, trading some energy density for longer cycle life and better thermal stability.
  • Panasonic, based in Japan, also supplies a 2170 cylindrical cell for a portion of production; which cars get which battery can be identified by the first three digits of the vehicle identification number (VIN).

2. FSD computer chip — Samsung Electronics

Tesla's Full Self-Driving computer runs on a chip built on Samsung Foundry's 14nm process, containing two neural processing units (NPUs) that handle the real-time compute load for autonomous driving features.

3. Tires — Hankook Tire

EV-specific tires need a different design than gas-car tires: EVs are heavier (from the battery pack) and instant-torque electric motors put different stress on tread, so EV tire lines prioritize low rolling resistance (for range) and low noise (since there's no engine noise to mask road noise). Hankook Tire's business filings list EV-specific tire lines among its products.

How to read EV supply-chain stocks

A car has thousands of parts, but not all of them move a stock's story the same way. Battery cells are the highest-value, highest-margin component in an EV and the one automakers actively multi-source to manage risk and cost — which is exactly why Tesla runs three separate suppliers on one model. Chips and tires matter too, but they're shared more broadly across the auto industry rather than being EV-specific bets.

FAQ

Which Korean stocks are linked to the Tesla Model Y?
LG Energy Solution (battery cells), Samsung Electronics (FSD chip, Samsung Foundry), and Hankook Tire (tires) are the three Korea-listed companies with disclosed or filed ties to Model Y-type components. CATL and Panasonic, the other two battery suppliers, are not Korea-listed.

Are all three battery suppliers confirmed by Tesla?
Yes. Tesla has publicly disclosed using LG Energy Solution, CATL, and Panasonic across different Model Y trims and production batches.

Is the FSD chip supplier confirmed by Tesla?
Samsung Foundry's 14nm process for Tesla's FSD chip has been publicly disclosed by Samsung; we did not find a Tesla-side confirmation naming Samsung specifically for the Model Y.

Is the video a real teardown?
No. It is a reconstruction based on public information.

Summary

  • 2170 cylindrical cell (NCM): LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220)
  • Prismatic LFP cell: CATL (China)
  • 2170 cylindrical cell: Panasonic (Japan)
  • FSD computer chip: Samsung Electronics (KRX: 005930)
  • Tires: Hankook Tire (KRX: 000240)

Sources: Tesla's public battery-supplier disclosures; Samsung's Samsung Foundry process disclosures; Hankook Tire and Samsung Electronics business reports filed with Korea's DART system.
The companies listed make these types of parts; Tesla has confirmed only the battery suppliers publicly. Images and video are reconstructions, not a physical teardown. This post summarizes public information and is not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
